sn48.64:1.1: The discourses [sn48.61]()–64 follow the same template as [sn54.19]()–20. In both series, we have the fetters, underlying tendencies, course of time, and end of defilements as individual items, then a final passage that combines all four items. We find the same basic series also at [sn45.42]()–45, but without the combined list. The editing in different editions exhibits considerable uncertainty. In the MS edition, for example, the current Sutta lists the final four in one sentence, whereas at [sn54.20:1.8]() they are separated by ellipsis, showing that the editors thought some passages had been elided. BJT, on the other hand spells out the main four passages in full, but omits the combined series entirely. At [sn54.20]() it says, “these three discourses should also be expanded just as the discourse on the fetters”. However it has, in fact, just spelled all of the discourses in full, rendering the instructions moot, so they must be a holdover from one of the sources from which the BJT was edited.
sn48.64:1.4: The close _-ti_ here indicates that, following the pattern of the previous three discourses, the Sutta ends here. This is in fact the reading in BJT. The PTS, followed by Bodhi, omits this closing statement and continues as if it were the same Sutta. The same template is followed at [sn54.19]()–20, In fact the next passage should belong to a separate sutta, but we follow the MS edition. BB omits this close statement in his translation, thus giving the impression that the sutta continues. In this he evidently follows the Sinhala reading via the PTS. However the Burmese readings are more coherent.
